clue.text: Check those printing religious tracts?

definitions.meaning: to check an urge or a rebellion is to hold it down or stifle it
a press, a printing house, turning out material for Religious Education

explanation.surface: A question about whether to curb the people who print religious pamphlets.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE (Religious Education, a British school subject) plus PRESS, a printing house; the question mark flags this playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or suppress it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Update troops before attack

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army troops
a fit is an attack, as in a coughing fit

explanation.surface: Bring soldiers up to date before an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit is to re-equip or modernise, as when a ship or shop is updated.

clue.text: An account traveller set, up providing support for climbers

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the pieces are written bottom to top

parts.note: a log is a record or account
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: Someone's report of a travelling salesman setting up a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set, up' is the reversal signal; 'set' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework over which climbing plants grow.

clue.text: Liberal prone to adopting Conservative hairstyle

indicators.note: adopting takes something in, so the letter goes inside
liberal means free or loose, so the following letters are treated freely and reordered

parts.note: C, abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A left-leaning type inclined to take on a Tory haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts C inside ETONROP, the rearranged letters of PRONE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton crop is a short sleek women's haircut fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Crowd security?

parts.note: the protection one gets from being part of a large group, not stewards at a match

explanation.surface: Stewards and police keeping a crowd safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one is safer as one of many than alone, the protection a crowd offers.

clue.text: Beaten revolutionary featured in flyer

indicators.note: a person featured in a picture appears within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bird is a flyer
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel pictured in a pilot's story has been thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone birched has been flogged with a bundle of twigs, so beaten in the physical sense.

clue.text: Case based on word of chap, or chaps, before I'm involved

definitions.text: Case based on word of chap

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawsuit hinging on one man's pledge, with Is and chaps tangled in.
explanation.walkthrough: This was formerly a lawsuit brought when a man broke off an engagement, his word to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal action rested on a fiancé's broken undertaking to wed, his word given.

clue.text: Treasury theatre put on old romance with current investment

parts.note: rep, repertory theatre
O, abbreviation for old

indicators.note: investment as in besieging or enclosing, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: a romance is a story
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A finance ministry puts on an old love tale while also investing.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a store where valuables are kept, like a treasury.

clue.text: His friend has Hamlet's first speech abridged

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Hamlet's
abridged means shortened, so the last letter of the word for speech goes

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A friend gets the opening lines of Hamlet's soliloquy cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back through the clue to Hamlet, Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal companion and confidant in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Doctor gets a payment covering time he has to serve in US

definitions.text: he has to serve in US

parts.note: DR, abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the letter for time goes inside

parts.note: a fee is a payment
T, abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A doctor gets paid for his hours of service.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is an American conscript, someone drafted for military service.

clue.text: How sugar can be used, if at all?

definitions.meaning: sugar is boiled down to make a sweet, being used in that confection
the idiom 'can't do it ...' means cannot do it at all

explanation.surface: A cook wondering whether sugar has any use whatsoever.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'can't do something for toffee' means being hopeless at it; the 'if' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sugar goes towards a chewy sweet; idiomatically the phrase means in any way at all.

clue.text: Chest protected by father's waterproof

indicators.note: something protected by another is wrapped round by it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Pa is father, and the 's stands for 'is', a link
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A trunk kept safe beneath dad's rain jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded anorak, a jacket that keeps the rain out, so a waterproof as a noun.

clue.text: Brought books back on approval

indicators.note: back means the books abbreviation is read from its end to its start

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Someone returned library books after they were given the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Took and brought are both past tenses of carrying something somewhere, as in took a present to her.

clue.text: Perseveres and catches a little bird

parts.note: a drawer that catches jams, i.e. sticks
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going and finally nets a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at a task without giving up is the idiom 'to stick at it'.

clue.text: Tense liar added ridiculous nonsense

parts.note: T, the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters are made a nonsense of and rearranged

explanation.surface: An uptight fibber has tacked on absurd rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Taradiddle is an old word for pretentious nonsense or a petty lie.

clue.text: Gulf national sounding full of cold

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that, said out loud, matches the one given

parts.note: catarrhy describes someone full of catarrh, the mucus of a heavy cold

explanation.surface: A person from the Gulf whose voice is thick with a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A Qatari is a citizen of Qatar, a state on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Brexiteers asking for this defeat on polling day

definitions.meaning: those wanting Britain to leave the EU campaigned for a ballot to go OUT
to beat a rival by gaining more ballots

explanation.surface: Leave campaigners hoping for an election win over their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: Brexiteers are people who backed the UK leaving the European Union in the 2016 referendum; they wanted an 'Out' result.
explanation.definitionFit: To outvote someone is to beat them by having more ballots cast for you.

clue.text: Bear from America digging into soil

indicators.note: something digging into another burrows inside it, so one piece goes within

parts.note: to soil is to stain
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A bear from America rooting around in the dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to hold it up or endure it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rebellious graduates wash thoroughly one day a week

indicators.note: rebellious means revolting, turning over, so the word for graduates is reversed upward

parts.note: BAs, Bachelors of Arts
a bath is a thorough wash

explanation.surface: Unruly students have a proper scrub once every seven days.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest and worship.

clue.text: Injured Danes coming aboard in gloom

indicators.note: coming aboard means getting inside, so the letters go within the ship letters

parts.note: aboard means on a ship, SS (steamship) round the rest

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Wounded Danes being taken onto a vessel in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom and sadness both mean low spirits or melancholy.

clue.text: Most utter support after turning up

indicators.note: after places the word for support behind the turned piece
turning means the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: a rest is a support, like an armrest

explanation.surface: A prop that has been flipped over and pointed upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute or complete, so the most utter is the purest, as in purest nonsense.

clue.text: Abject drunk lives without ever losing heart

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
drunk means tipsy and unsteady, so the letters of lives stagger into a new order
losing heart means the middle letters of ever are removed

explanation.surface: A wretched drinker carries on, never once discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject can mean grovelling and slavish, which is what servile means.

clue.text: Bloke gets the way things are done in small part of Cornwall

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person, a bloke

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for method inside the word for small

parts.note: minor means small
MO, modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A man learns the local customs in a little corner of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodmin Moor is a granite upland region in the middle of that county.

clue.text: See 3
What diver may do with bill, on cutting pound

definitions.text: What diver may do with bill

indicators.note: cutting into means a piece breaks open the other and sits within

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen
RE means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A swimmer counts the cost of an invoice while cutting it down.
explanation.walkthrough: A diver here is a bird, a diving waterfowl, and the bill its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their feathers with their beaks, which is preening.

clue.text: Employment from IT entrepreneur?

definitions.meaning: Steve, co-founder of Apple, a computing businessman

explanation.surface: Work generated by a tech businessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment means work or positions; Steve of Apple fame bore this surname.

clue.text: Each individually at an advantage

definitions.meaning: per person, so much a head

explanation.surface: Every one separately has the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of competitors gives a lead; 'a head' also means per person, as in a fee per head.

clue.text: Sum up chapter cut from historic volume one's penned

indicators.note: cut from means the abbreviation for chapter is removed from the word for historic

parts.note: epic, of heroic or historic scale

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: a tome is a large volume
I'S, one is, written IS

explanation.surface: Summarising a long history book after one chapter has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to give the essence of something, to summarise it concisely.

clue.text: Speeds up in speech, as ten strikes

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone talks faster as the clock chimes ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' looks like a signal for a sound-alike, but 'in' is the extraction signal and 'speech' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry or quicken, a straight synonym of speed up.

clue.text: Oriental crane ultimately like seabird

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of crane

parts.note: as means like
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An Asian crane that resembles a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe the East, especially Asia.
